msContents.summary: This work appears to be an Italian version of the treatise by Bernhardus, first published in Latin, at Bäle in 1583, but there are considerable differences both in the text and in the order of the contents.

msItem.author: Trevisanus, Bernhardus (1406-1490)
msItem.title: Il Libro Pietra Filosofale
msItem.incipit: Fol 1 Inconmencia [sic] il libro del Reverendo padre dottore nelle sacre/letre [sic] bernardo allemanno conte della Marca triuigiana/Inuocando il nome del signore...
msItem.explicit: Fol 27 Finisce il libro del spaientissimo filosofo Bernardo/Conte de treues in Alemagna [sic] mandato al/nobile Dottore tomaso da Bolognia gouernator/di francia.
msItem.filiation: For an account of the Author and his works, see Thorndike's History of Magic and Experimental Science, Vol. III, pp. 618-626, and Ferguson's 'Bibliotheca Chemica, Vol. I, pp. 101-104, Vol. II, pp. 496-467.

Research by Didier Kahn has established that the author is a fictional character and never existed. The chapter is from 2003 and titled “Recherches sur le Livre attribué au prétendu Bernard le Trévisan (fin du XVe siècle)”, en: Chiara Crisciani & Agostino Paravicini Bagliani (eds.) Alchimia e medicina nel Medioevo, SISMEL – Edizioni del Galluzzo, Firenze, pp. 265-336. Kahn argues that he is confused with a real person, Bernard of Trier (Bernard de Trèves), that Trevis' works have no verifiable facts and that his title and identity are contradictory.
